record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: Among precision neutron and nuclear beta-decay studies used to test electroweak interactions and search for beyond-Standard-Model couplings, which experimental systems and observables are most sensitive to the currently limiting unknowns? The comparison should cover the systems highlighted for modern beta decay, including neutron decay, superallowed 0+ -> 0+ Fermi transitions, mirror transitions within isospin T = 1/2 doublets, T = 1 Gamow-Teller decays, and observables such as beta-spectrum shapes, integrated decay rates, angular correlations, and recoil spectroscopy.

evidence.quote: We attempt to report on the current status of the following questions: 1. What systems and observables are most sensitive to current unknowns?

The choice of system is typically determined via the simplicity of its theoretical description (meaning the lowest degree of theoretical uncertainty due to, e.g., nuclear structure) and potential enhancements it provides in any of its observables. In the past, these have traditionally focused on allowed Fermi or Gamow-Teller decays such as the neutron, superallowed (SA) 0+ → 0+ Fermi transitions, mirror transitions within an isospin T = 1/2 doublet, and pure Gamow-Teller transitions within an T = 1 triplet.

Much success has been garnered from integrated quantities such as the total decay rate and angular correlations where one can construct (super-)ratios of numbers of counts in a detector array to compensate several systematic effects to first order leading to improved precision.

In the last decade, substantial focus has been diverted again to direct spectroscopy measurements due to linear rather than quadratic sensitivity to small exotic couplings in the Fierz interference term showing up as a 1 /Ee distortion to the β spectrum. On the other hand, following the success of ion and atom traps, precision recoil spectroscopy is once more becoming an interesting experimental system with the advent of novel technologies.

artifact.category_tag: precision beta-decay tests of the electroweak Standard Model
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open survey-style research question regarding the current frontier of precision β-decay experiments. Recent reviews (2023–2025) on Vud extraction, CKM unitarity, and BSM searches in β decay continue to treat the relative sensitivity of these systems and observables as an evolving open issue, with active competing programs in neutron decay (e.g. UCNA+, Nab, PERC), superallowed Fermi transitions (Ft survey updates), mirror decays, and trap-based recoil spectroscopy. No single definitive ranking is established in the literature.
